name: @gyral/mcp

tools.name: start_here
tools.description: Call this first, once per task. A short orientation for Gyral 0.3.3: the mental model, the rules agents most often break, the recommended workflow, which tool to use when, and an index from use case (form, fetch, search, routing, SSR, …) to the example and guide to start from. Gyral workflow: start_here once; start from get_example or scaffold_component; write a minimal implementation; check_snippet it and apply the suggested fixes until it passes; use get_api only to look up one specific symbol.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the Gyral 0.3.3 documentation (guides, API reference, examples) for one concept you need. Returns ranked sections with their URL; pass a URL to get_doc for the full text. Don't read the docs end to end before writing code. Gyral workflow: start_here once; start from get_example or scaffold_component; write a minimal implementation; check_snippet it and apply the suggested fixes until it passes; use get_api only to look up one specific symbol.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. "hydrate island" or "formAction 422".

tools.name: get_doc
tools.description: Returns one docs page as markdown, or one section when the reference has a #anchor (prefer a section: pages are long). Accepts a URL (https://gyral.dev/docs/forms/#the-server-half), a path (/docs/intent/) or a short name (intent, forms#the-server-half, api/core, examples). Gyral workflow: start_here once; start from get_example or scaffold_component; write a minimal implementation; check_snippet it and apply the suggested fixes until it passes; use get_api only to look up one specific symbol.

path_or_url.description: URL, path or page name, optionally with #anchor.

tools.name: get_api
tools.description: Declaration, doc comment and import path of one public @gyral/* export (e.g. define, form, renderPage, step) you are about to use. A miss suggests the nearest export names, and for an unexported helper type says how to name it. Not for browsing the type graph: start from get_example or scaffold_component instead. Pass "*" to list every export, optionally for one package. Gyral workflow: start_here once; start from get_example or scaffold_component; write a minimal implementation; check_snippet it and apply the suggested fixes until it passes; use get_api only to look up one specific symbol.

symbol.description: Exported name, e.g. "define", or "*" for the index.

package.description: Limit to a package or entry point: "core", "@gyral/ssr/static".

tools.name: list_examples
tools.description: Every runnable example in the Gyral repo with what it demonstrates. Read the closest one with get_example and adapt it. Gyral workflow: start_here once; start from get_example or scaffold_component; write a minimal implementation; check_snippet it and apply the suggested fixes until it passes; use get_api only to look up one specific symbol.

tools.name: get_example
tools.description: Workflow step 1: working code to start from. An example's description, link and the full source of its component files (start_here maps use cases to examples). Adapt it into a minimal implementation right away. Gyral workflow: start_here once; start from get_example or scaffold_component; write a minimal implementation; check_snippet it and apply the suggested fixes until it passes; use get_api only to look up one specific symbol.

tools.name: scaffold_component
tools.description: Workflow step 1: idiomatic starting code that imports only packages the project has installed (read from the project's package.json). "basic" (state, intents, pure update, view; a model test when @gyral/testing and vitest are installed), "form" (with valibot or zod 4 installed: a schema shared with the server; otherwise the dependency-free form), "form-native" (no dependencies: novalidate plus the browser's constraint checks, custom messages, focus on the first invalid field), "ssr-page" (light-DOM page, client entry, and a server route when @gyral/ssr is installed). Adapt it into a minimal implementation right away. Gyral workflow: start_here once; start from get_example or scaffold_component; write a minimal implementation; check_snippet it and apply the suggested fixes until it passes; use get_api only to look up one specific symbol.

tag.description: Custom element name with a hyphen, e.g. "todo-list".

description.description: What the component should do (added as a comment).

project_dir.description: The project whose package.json says what is installed (default: the server's project directory). Relative paths start there.

installed.description: Package names the project has installed, e.g. ["@gyral/core", "vitest", "@gyral/testing", "valibot"]. Added to what package.json says; without either, only @gyral/core is assumed.

tools.name: check_snippet
tools.description: Workflow step 3, after writing code: typechecks a TypeScript module against the project's installed TypeScript and @gyral/* types (the server's working directory, or GYRAL_PROJECT_DIR) and returns each error with a suggested fix, plus common Gyral mistakes TypeScript can't see (one-call define, listen in init, periodic, side effects in update, handlers in views, rows without a TemplateResult return type). Apply the fixes and call it again until it passes. Use it before presenting Gyral code. Gyral workflow: start_here once; start from get_example or scaffold_component; write a minimal implementation; check_snippet it and apply the suggested fixes until it passes; use get_api only to look up one specific symbol.

code.description: A complete TypeScript module, imports included.

instructions: Gyral builds web components as Model-View-Intent loops with their own view layer (html, css, each, prop from @gyral/core): intent parses DOM events into typed messages, update is one pure reducer per message, view is a pure function of state that names intents with data-intent (no event handlers), and side effects are commands performed by drivers. Call start_here first (the orientation, also in the gyral://skill resource). Then start from get_example or scaffold_component, write a minimal implementation right away, and verify it; use get_api only to look up one specific symbol, and search_docs / get_doc for one concept you need. Run check_snippet on every file, apply its suggested fixes and check again until it passes before answering.
